cards.name: Prefer the option whose active ingredient is already named in the dialogue
cards.applies_when: The dialogue explicitly names a medication or active ingredient, and the answer options include both that exact active ingredient and a different drug from the same therapeutic class or with a similar indication.
cards.exclude_when: The dialogue names a medication only as a current medication that is being investigated as a possible cause or interacting factor, and the question asks for a new treatment for the suspected diagnosis; or the named medication is not a plausible treatment for the diagnosis under discussion.
cards.procedure: 1. Identify the active ingredient explicitly named in the dialogue. 2. Check whether it appears as an answer option. 3. If it does, and the question is asking for the treatment/medication most consistent with the dialogue, choose that option over same-class alternatives. 4. If the named medication is only a possible exacerbating factor or is not indicated for the diagnosis, do not apply this rule.

cards.name: Prefer the option that matches the diagnosis-specific drug class over a same-class alternative
cards.applies_when: The dialogue supports a specific diagnosis, and the answer options include two drugs from the same broad therapeutic area but only one is the standard first-line or diagnosis-specific agent for that diagnosis.
cards.exclude_when: The dialogue does not clearly support the diagnosis, or the two same-class options are both equally appropriate for the diagnosis, or the patient has a contraindication that makes the standard agent unsafe.
cards.procedure: 1. Determine the most likely diagnosis from the dialogue. 2. Identify the drug class or mechanism most directly indicated for that diagnosis. 3. Among same-class options, choose the one that is the standard first-line or most specific treatment for the diagnosis. 4. Do not choose a same-class alternative merely because it is also used in the broader disease area.
